To make the conversation concrete, can you confirm roughs for: average tokens per user request, % of sessions that require >8k context, and expected steady concurrency (api calls/sec) during peak clinic hours? If you prefer, Raj (cc'd) can share telemetry or a short sample.

I'll loop in Karthik (solutions) and Marissa (sales-eng) to provide a preliminary GPU sizing and cost delta (fp16 vs int8) ahead of the call. If we can get those numbers today we can deliver a recommended reserved capacity and a short amortized monthly cost for the deal team.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: DeltaCare dedicated capacity: memory footprint, KV cache & quantization trade-offs

Elena / team —

Thanks for the numbers, very helpful. Quick technical summary and conservative sizing so procurement has firm numbers:

- Workload profile (using your inputs): avg request 420 tokens, 22% sessions >16k, peak concurrency 85 reqs. We model an average sequence-length distribution: 70% <=2048, 8% between 2049-8192, 22% >8192 (up to 32k in rare cases).

- KV cache impact: For long-context sessions we keep a per-session KV cache for up to 30 minutes of activity. The KV working set per session grows roughly linearly with prefix length; for a 16k context on our reference LLM (2.7B transformer variant with 1 KV per token) we estimate ~6.6 GB of GPU memory consumed in KV cache per concurrent long session (fp16).

- Model memory (weights): reference fp16 weights ~12.8 GB; int8 quantization reduces weight resident footprint to ~6.8 GB (note: depends on quant backend + calibration; we recommend q4_0 or int8 with per-channel calibration for minimal quality delta).

- Combined per-concurrent-session working set (conservative):
  - fp16 baseline: weights (12.8 GB) + per-long-session KV (6.6 GB) + activation overhead (~2.2 GB) => ~21.6 GB for a GPU serving a single long session.
  - int8 path: weights (6.8 GB) + KV (6.6 GB) + activation overhead (~2.2 GB) => ~15.6 GB.

- Concurrency mapping to GPU count: with continuous batching and session affinity, an A100 40GB can sustain ~3 concurrent long sessions (fp16) or ~4 concurrent long sessions (int8) assuming our batching latency SLO (95th <= 450ms). For short sessions (<=2k) the A100 can handle ~18-22 qps depending on prompt shapes. T4 16GB cards are possible if you commit to int8 and accept lower concurrency (~1 long session per GPU, higher latency tail).

- Recommended reserved commit (conservative for your peak 85 concurrent requests and mix):
  1) If we can standardize on int8 for the main pipeline: reserve 10 x A100-40GB (gives headroom for growth and failover) — estimated amortized monthly cost shown in attached workbook.
  2) If int8 is not approved and we must run fp16: reserve 18 x A100-40GB (or hybrid: 12 A100 + 20 T4 for lower-priority routes).

Risk/tradeoffs: int8 reduces GPU count and cost materially but requires a short calibration pass and a small eval set to verify summarization fidelity. We can run a blinded A/B on a subset of clinical notes to validate no clinically material regressions; this is standard for other healthcare customers.

Next steps: 1) can DeltaCare provide a 1k-record evaluation set (redacted) we can run through int8 calibration; 2) agree on an initial reserved capacity option to put in the draft SOW so procurement has numbers. I'm happy to run a 30-minute technical session tomorrow to walk through the math.

-Karthik

Option A (recommended, if int8 approved): 10 x A100-40GB reserved (SLA: 99.95% uptime, 95th latency target 450ms) — includes dedicated KV cache sizing and a canary pipeline for fp16 fallbacks.

Option B (fp16 baseline): 18 x A100-40GB reserved (SLA: 99.98% uptime) or hybrid mix we can outline if you'd like lower cost.

Procurement asks we usually see: committed minimums, termination windows, and a 30-day QA eval run for quantization. If DeltaCare is comfortable with Option A we can generate a draft SOW and MSA numbers for Alicia.

Marissa — please prepare the official quote and include the int8 calibration and QA run as a line item. Karthik — please prepare the evaluation checklist for clinical validation.
